Theja Rio's debut feature Angh won the Platform Prize at TIFF 2026 on Sunday. It was the only Indian film in the Platform competition, up against 11 others.

The jury praised its "vision, audacity and courage".

Dor released 20 years ago today, and it's still a hidden gem.

Nagesh Kukunoor, 22 September 2006. Gul Panag's Zeenat has one way to save her husband from execution abroad: the victim's widow has to forgive him.

Two women, one decision, and nobody you can easily hate.

The Shawshank Redemption opened in the US 32 years ago today, on 23 September 1994. It flopped.

About $16 million in its first run, on a $25 million budget. Seven Oscar nominations, zero wins.
Then it became America's most-rented film of 1995, and cable reruns from 1997 did the rest. The Library of Congress preserved it in 2015.
From a 96-page Stephen King novella. Frank Darabont wrote and directed.

Prem Chopra turns 91 today.

Born in Lahore on 23 September 1935, he started as the hero of a Punjabi film, Chaudhary Karnail Singh, in 1960.

text:
Flopped. Then classic.

Shawshank opened 32 years ago today and lost money. Hindi cinema has its own list:
1959 Kaagaz Ke Phool: India's first CinemaScope film and a box-office bomb. Guru Dutt never officially directed again.
1970 Mera Naam Joker: Raj Kapoor's four-hour epic. It failed; a shorter cut did well in the '80s.
1994 Andaz Apna Apna: flopped, and now everyone quotes it.
2004 Swades: a commercial disappointment that's now called one of Shah Rukh Khan's best.

Thuppakki (2012): Vijay, and only the second Tamil film to cross ₹100 crore in India.
Kaththi (2014): his Filmfare Best Director.
Sikandar (2025): with Salman Khan.

Ilaiyaraaja's 50th-anniversary tour plays Sydney on 26 September. Days earlier, Victoria's Parliament honoured him with a ceremonial stamp marking 50 years in cinema.

Mouna Ragam, Nayakan, Thalapathi with Mani Ratnam. Cheeni Kum and Paa in Hindi.

text:
Four films. No misses.

Before Jailer 2 on 15 October, every Nelson Dilipkumar film so far. He started as a scriptwriter at Star Vijay, and Anirudh has scored all of them.
Kolamaavu Kokila (2018): Nayanthara, a dark comedy, and a hit debut.
Doctor (2021): deadpan Sivakarthikeyan, and one of the biggest Tamil hits after cinemas reopened.
Beast (2022): Vijay, a hijacked mall, Arabic Kuthu.
Jailer (2023): Rajinikanth, over ₹600 crore worldwide.
Next: Jailer 2, then KHxRK (working title) with Kamal Haasan and Rajinikanth.

Which one's his best?

text:
Avril Lavigne turns 42 today.

Born 27 September 1984 in Belleville, Ontario. Her debut Let Go (2002) gave us "Complicated" and "Sk8er Boi", sold over 16 million copies by 2009, and is still the best-selling album of the century by a Canadian artist.
Seven studio albums and eight Grammy nominations later, the tie-and-tank-top era is still how most of us picture her.
Complicated or Sk8er Boi?

text:
The King of Romance was born today.

Yash Chopra, born 27 September 1932. He founded Yash Raj Films in 1970 and made stars for five decades.
Deewaar (1975): locked in Amitabh Bachchan's stardom.
Silsila (1981): one love triangle, and "Rang Barse" at every Holi since.
Chandni (1989): Sridevi, chiffon, Switzerland.
Darr (1993): Shah Rukh Khan as the obsessive one.
Dil To Pagal Hai (1997): the highest-grossing Hindi film of its year.
Interlaken made him an honorary ambassador in 2011, and there's a statue of him there now.

text:
Why have you not seen Lamhe?

Of all the films he directed, Lamhe (1991) was Yash Chopra's own favourite. Sridevi plays a double role, a mother and, years later, her daughter, with Anil Kapoor, Waheeda Rehman and Anupam Kher.
It did modest business in India and better overseas, then won Filmfare Best Film. In 2013 it made a list of the top 10 romantic films from Indian cinema's first 100 years.
"Ahead of its time" is usually a cliché. Here it's just accurate.

text:
Madonna opens the VMAs. Again.

It's her first VMA performance in 23 years and a record fifth time opening the show. The history:
1984: at the very first VMAs, "Like a Virgin" in a wedding dress, on a giant wedding cake.
1998: "Ray of Light" with Lenny Kravitz on guitar, and five Moonmen the same night.
2003: Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera as brides and Madonna as the groom. That was her last VMA performance, until this one.
2026: most-nominated artist (13). The show is Monday 5 AM in India.
Best VMA moment ever?

Naomi Watts turns 58. Here's the film that made her.

Mulholland Drive (2001). David Lynch shot it as a TV pilot for ABC; ABC passed, so he made it a film. Watts plays two women, hopeful Betty and wrecked Diane. Lynch won Best Director at Cannes, and a 2016 BBC critics' poll named it the best film of the 21st century.

text:
Amitabh Bachchan called him godfather.

Mehmood was born on 29 September 1932 in Bombay. Over 300 films, and a habit of giving other people their big break.
1943: started as a child in Kismet, the first Indian film to earn ₹1 crore.
1961: produced Chhote Nawab, R. D. Burman's first film as composer.
1968: produced Padosan and played Master Pillai.
1972: co-produced Bombay to Goa and gave Amitabh Bachchan the lead.
Four Filmfares for Best Comedian. And his son is Lucky Ali.

text:
Mind-bender: Memento.

Christopher Nolan's second film (2000). Guy Pearce's Leonard can't make new memories, so he hunts his wife's killer with Polaroids and tattoos. The colour scenes run in reverse, the black-and-white ones run forward, and they meet at the end.
Two Oscar nominations. And A.R. Murugadoss borrowed its 15-minute memory man for Ghajini.
Buzzora verdict: watch it once for the twist. Twice for the trick.

text:
Hindi cinema's kindest director was born today.

Hrishikesh Mukherjee was born on 30 September 1922 in Calcutta. 42 films, eight Filmfares, and almost no villains. Four to start with:
1971: Anand. Rajesh Khanna laughs; Amitabh Bachchan can't.
1973: Abhimaan. A singer marries a better singer. Amitabh and Jaya Bachchan married that year.
1975: Chupke Chupke. Dharmendra as a professor pretending to be a driver.
1979: Gol Maal. Amol Palekar invents a clean-shaven twin, and wins the Filmfare for Best Actor.
Before all of it he was an editor, on Bimal Roy's Do Bigha Zamin. Dadasaheb Phalke Award, 1999.
Your Hrishida film?

text:
Tom Cruise, standing still.

His Friday film, Digger, is an Iñárritu comedy. He's been great without a stunt before. Five to start with:
1988: Rain Man. A hustler meets the brother he never knew he had (Dustin Hoffman). Best Picture.
1989: Born on the Fourth of July. Oliver Stone; his first Oscar nomination.
1999: Magnolia. Paul Thomas Anderson's sleazy dating guru. A Golden Globe win.
1999: Eyes Wide Shut. Stanley Kubrick's last film, with Nicole Kidman.
2008: Tropic Thunder. Les Grossman, under a bald cap.
Then Digger, in cinemas Friday, 2 October. Your best non-running Cruise?

18 awards abroad. Now, India.

Vinod Kapri's Pyre opens in Indian cinemas on Friday, 23 October, through Cinépolis. It follows an elderly couple in a Kumaon Himalayan village, and the children who left for the cities. The leads are first-time actors: Padam Singh Kapri, 80, and Heera Devi, 70. Oscar winner Mychael Danna (Life of Pi) scores it; Gulzar writes the lyrics. It premiered at Tallinn Black Nights, where it won the audience award for best film.

He left a royal family. For music.

S. D. Burman was born 120 years ago today, on 1 October 1906, in Comilla, into Tripura's royal family. He scored about 89 Hindi films. Four to start with:
1957: Pyaasa. Guru Dutt's unpublished poet; Waheeda Rehman as Gulabo.
1965: Guide. "Wahan Kaun Hai Tera" is Burman's own voice.
1969: Aradhana. "Mere Sapnon Ki Rani", and a National Award for his singing on "Safal Hogi Teri Aradhana".
1973: Abhimaan. His second Filmfare for Best Music.
His son R. D. Burman took it from there.

Why have you not seen Thevar Magan?

Sivaji Ganesan was born on this day in 1928. Start with the film he made with Kamal Haasan in 1992: a London-educated son comes home with city plans, and his father, the village chief, needs him to stay. Kamal wrote and produced it; Bharathan directed. It won five National Awards and was India's Oscar entry. Sivaji refused the jury's special award.
Watch it for the father. Stay for the son.

Hollywood once said no to Julie Andrews.

She turns 91 today. The role she lost, and four that made up for it:
1956: My Fair Lady. She created Eliza on Broadway; Jack Warner cast Audrey Hepburn in the film.

Now: Lady Whistledown's voice in Bridgerton, which won her an Emmy at 89.

He quit at his peak. To garden in Oregon.

Vinod Khanna was born 80 years ago today, on 6 October 1946, in Peshawar. Five turns in one career:
1971: Mere Apne. His first lead, in Gulzar's film, opposite Shatrughan Sinha.
1977: Amar Akbar Anthony. He was Amar, the police officer.
1980: Qurbani. Feroz Khan's hit, the one with "Aap Jaisa Koi".
1982: He left films for Rajneeshpuram, Osho's commune in Oregon, as Swami Vinod Bharti. He worked as a gardener.
1987: Insaaf brought him back. Then Chandni, Dabangg, four terms as Gurdaspur's MP and a Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2017).

Cinema learned to talk today.

The Jazz Singer premiered in New York on 6 October 1927, 99 years ago.
It had about two minutes of synchronised talking. Al Jolson's first line: "Wait a minute, wait a minute, you ain't heard nothin' yet!"
Sam Warner, the Warner brother who pushed hardest for sound, died the day before the premiere.
India took four more years. Ardeshir Irani's Alam Ara opened at the Majestic Cinema, Bombay, on 14 March 1931.
Its "De De Khuda Ke Naam Pe" is counted as Hindi cinema's first song.
No print of Alam Ara survives. In 2017 the BFI called it the most important lost Indian film.
One lost film you'd bring back?

Five Indian horror films that actually scare.

It's October. Skip the horror-comedies for one night.
Raaz (2002): Vikram Bhatt's haunted-house hit, with Bipasha Basu and Dino Morea.
Bulbbul (2020, Netflix): Anvita Dutt's gothic fable, with Tripti Dimri.
Pari (2018): Anushka Sharma produced it and starred.
13B (2009): Madhavan, a new flat and a TV serial that seems to know his family's future. In Tamil it's Yavarum Nalam.
Bhoot (2003): Ram Gopal Varma's haunted flat, and Urmila Matondkar's possession scenes.
Bonus: Bramayugam (2024), the role that won Mammootty his fourth National Award.

text:
This horror film speaks a language that doesn't exist.

The language is Boksirit, built from scratch by Dutch linguist Jan van Steenbergen. THR India says Bokshi is only the second Indian feature, after Baahubali, to have one.
Bokshi opens in cinemas today, 9 October. It's Bhargav Saikia's first feature: a troubled teenager, Anahita (Prasanna Bisht), joins a school trek to a remote prehistoric site and finds a link to an old legend. Mansi Multani plays her history teacher. It's in Hindi, Nepali and English, plus Boksirit, and it's set in Sikkim.
It premiered at Rotterdam in 2025, then played Sitges, Neuchâtel and SXSW Sydney.
Baahubali had Kiliki. Bokshi has Boksirit. Watching it this weekend?

The oldest surviving film is 138 today.

Louis Le Prince shot Roundhay Garden Scene in a garden in Roundhay, Leeds, on 14 October 1888: four people walking, about two seconds long, on his own single-lens camera.
In September 1890 he boarded a train from Dijon to Paris and was never seen again.

Richard Carpenter is 80. The other Carpenter.

Karen sang. Richard, born 15 October 1946, built the sound around her voice.
"(They Long to Be) Close to You" went to No. 1 in the US in July 1970 and stayed four weeks.
"We've Only Just Begun" reached No. 2 three months later. Paul Williams and Roger Nichols first wrote it for a bank commercial.
Karen started as the band's drummer. Richard put her out front to sing, and wrote the arrangements.
"Top of the World" became their second US No. 1 in 1973. "Yesterday Once More", the same year, became their biggest hit worldwide.
More than 100 million records sold, and Best New Artist at the 1971 Grammys.

Udit Narayan sang the title song with Alka Yagnik, who won the National Award for Best Female Playback Singer.

Pakeezah took 15 years to make. Now it's back in 4K.

Kamal Amrohi wrote and directed it. Filming began in 1956; it premiered on 4 February 1972, with Meena Kumari as Sahibjaan and Raaj Kumar.
It started in black and white, then was reshot in colour and CinemaScope.
Ghulam Mohammed wrote the songs, Chalte Chalte among them, and died before release. Naushad finished the score.
Shivendra Singh Dungarpur's Film Heritage Foundation spent two years restoring it with the Amrohi family at L'Immagine Ritrovata, Bologna.
The 4K version premiered at the Festival Lumière in Lyon, then closed the 70th BFI London Film Festival at the BFI IMAX on 18 October. No Indian date yet.

Shah Rukh Khan's defining film? Variety says Devdas (2002). Five facts:

Aditya Sarpotdar's film has a ghost who wants a bride and sets his sights on Sharvari's Bela. Sathyaraj, Baahubali's Kattappa, plays Elvis, a quirky exorcist. Abhay Verma plays Bittu, the boy the ghost latches onto, and Mona Singh is his mother. Munjya crossed ₹100 crore at the box office.

In Yeh Prem Mol Liya she's opposite Ayushmann Khurrana.

Saroj Khan was born on this day in 1948. You know her steps.

Ek Do Teen · Tezaab (1988): Madhuri Dixit's breakout, and a Filmfare award for the choreography.
Hawa Hawai · Mr. India (1987): Sridevi at full comic tilt.
Dola Re Dola · Devdas (2002): Aishwarya Rai and Madhuri together, and a National Award.
Yeh Ishq Haaye · Jab We Met (2007): Kareena Kapoor, and another National Award.

Over 2,000 songs and three National Awards, from a career that began as a child artist. She died in 2020.

Which step can you still do?

IFFI 2026 opened in Goa on Friday, 20 November, and Kartik Aaryan said being there felt "like being at a fair", with so many films to watch. Sai Pallavi came in a mint-green silk saree.

Paweł Pawlikowski's Fatherland, which shared the best director prize at Cannes this year, opened the 57th festival. Ricky Kej led the music, and the theme is "Stories Without Borders". IFFI runs until 28 November.

And Kartik turns 36 today.

Jaideep Ahlawat has a new Netflix show, and Paatal Lok fans will know his co-star.

Pushpak Vimaan is a crime caper co-created and co-written by Sudip Sharma and Abhishek Banerjee, Paatal Lok's creator and its Hathoda Tyagi. Sudip Sharma directs. Jaideep, Abhishek and Barun Sobti lead the cast; Netflix announced them on 12 November.

IFFI's schedule had the first two episodes premiering in Goa on 21 November. Netflix hasn't announced a release date yet.

Prem Nazir and Sheela made about 130 films together as a lead pair. Guinness World Records lists it as the longest screen partnership.

Prem Nazir also holds a Guinness record for playing the lead in 724 films. He was born on 7 April 1926, and in his centenary year IFFI is screening Thulabharam (1968), his film with Sarada, as a tribute.
